facts.statement: The extinct penguin genus Pseudaptenodytes was described by Simpson in 1970.
The type species of the genus is Pseudaptenodytes macraei, while Pseudaptenodytes minor is a disputed species.
The genus Pseudaptenodytes contains the type species Pseudaptenodytes macraei.
facts.quote: The extinct penguin genus Pseudaptenodytes contains the type species P. macraei

facts.statement: Smaller bones found in the genus have been assigned to Pseudaptenodytes minor, though it is uncertain if they represent a distinct species or just younger individuals.
facts.quote: smaller bones have been assigned to P. minor, although it is not certain whether they are really from a different species or simply of younger individuals

facts.statement: Fossils of Pseudaptenodytes were found in Victoria, Australia, in deposits dating to the Late Miocene or Early Pliocene.
facts.quote: The fossils of Pseudaptenodytes have been found in deposits in Victoria (Australia) which are of Late Miocene or Early Pliocene age.

facts.statement: The genus Pseudaptenodytes belongs to the family Spheniscidae.
Pseudaptenodytes lived between 7.246 and 5.333 million years ago during the Messinian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Messinian to Messinian (7.246 to 5.333 million years ago)
